The query stack also shows the failure occurring while `collect_mod_item_types` is collecting the top-level module, so this is the strongest root-cause candidate.

The backtrace shows the actual panic is `attempted .def_id() on invalid res: Err` in `rustc_hir/src/def.rs:653`, so this file is the immediate invariant violation site. It likely turns an invalid resolved field/name into a hard panic instead of letting collection recover.

The query stack has `type_of` directly below `adt_def`, and this file computes item types for collected HIR owners. Since the crash happens while lowering the ADT `D`, this is the next most likely place where invalid field state becomes visible.

This file explicitly enforces item-level rules including `union-field` validation. The bug involves an invalid union/unnamed-field shape, so this is a plausible semantic gate that should have prevented the bad state before collection panicked.

This pass validates post-expansion AST structure before HIR lowering, including invalid item/type/impl/pattern forms left behind by parsing or macros. Because the reproducer uses an unsupported field form, this is a plausible place where malformed structure should have been rejected cleanly.

The reproduction also includes an `E0412` path-resolution failure for `Foo` in the log, and this pass owns late name resolution and invalid-resolution recovery. An invalid `Res` here could explain why `check_field` later panics on `def_id()`.

This file builds `ty::Generics` for HIR definitions during collection, including special forms like anonymous consts and closures. It is adjacent to the ADT collection path and could participate in how the malformed item reaches `adt_def`.

This module runs item well-formedness checking after collection. While less direct than the collection code, it is another semantic validation layer that could be expected to catch the bad field/union shape before deeper queries are forced.

The reproducer’s failure is triggered by item-level syntax involving a union/struct field, so the item parser is a distant but still relevant surface candidate. If the malformed field form were being represented inconsistently, this would be one of the earliest places it could originate.
